facts: A model for an analog programmable array processor (APAP) is bio-inspired.
A bio-inspired model for an analog programmable array processor (APAP) is based on studies on the vertebrate retina.
A bio-inspired model for an analog programmable array processor (APAP) has permitted the realization of complex programmable spatio-temporal dynamics in VLSI.
A bio-inspired model for an analog programmable array processor (APAP) mimics the way in which images are processed in the visual pathway.
A bio-inspired model for an analog programmable array processor (APAP) renders a feasible alternative for the implementation of early vision applications in standard technologies.
A prototype chip has been designed.
A prototype chip was fabricated in a 0.5 µm standard CMOS process.
Images are processed in the visual pathway.
Computing power per area is amongst the highest reported for a single chip.
The paper presents some experimental results.
The model is for an analog programmable array processor (APAP).
